sections.body: Artificial intelligence in legal work is the use of machine learning, natural language processing, and data systems to read, sort, draft, search, and predict across legal materials. In practice, it now helps review millions of documents for relevance and privilege, extract contract terms, flag risky clauses, assemble first drafts, and surface cases or statutes that match a fact pattern. Law firms and legal departments use it to manage intake, billing, matter staffing, and outside counsel spend, while compliance teams use it to map rules to controls. It also appears in trademark screening, patent landscaping, litigation analytics, and security reviews of AI systems themselves. The field is not one product but a set of workflows that touch the practice of law, the business of law, and the regulation of AI.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Document review and contract extraction are mature enough for routine use, with human review still needed for privilege, nuance, and final judgment. Legal research tools can retrieve and summarize, but they can miss authority, misread jurisdiction, or produce confident errors, so citations need checking. Prediction and judicial analytics remain contested, because outcomes depend on facts, procedure, and discretion that models often cannot see. The site currently tracks 149 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, which shows how quickly courts are being asked to define the rules. On the regulatory side, 7066 state AI bills and 220 compliance and regulation pages reflect a fast-moving patchwork rather than a settled body of law.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section divide the field by legal function and by the infrastructure that supports it. E-Discovery and Large-Scale Document Analysis covers review workflows and evidence handling, while Contract Lifecycle and Algorithmic Drafting follows agreements from intake to renewal. Legal Research and Case Strategy and Litigation Prediction and Judicial Analytics look at how AI supports argument, precedent, and forecasts, and Corporate Governance and Regulatory Compliance connects board duties to rule tracking. Intellectual Property and Trademark Strategy and Data Privacy and Cyber-Regulatory Compliance focus on two areas where AI creates both new tools and new exposure. Emerging Legal Frameworks follows the statutes, cases, and proposals being written now, and Legal Operations, Infrastructure and Security and AI Security Audits and Enterprise Enablement cover the internal systems, controls, and audits that let legal teams adopt AI without losing oversight.
